questions.question: What does this black and yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is one-way traffic only.
There is a detour to the right due to road construction.
The road ahead turns sharply at a steep angle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply at a steep angle.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions ahead. This sign warns you to slow down for a sharp turn in the road.

questions.question: When must you yield to a pedestrian?

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
At all times, even if they are breaking the law.
Only if the traffic light favors the pedestrian.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times, even if they are breaking the law.
questions.explanation: Always watch for pedestrians near your vehicle. You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter the situation.

questions.question: On a slippery road, how far should you stay behind the car ahead?

options.text: The same distance as on a normal road.
Farther back than normal.
Closer than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther back than normal.
questions.explanation: You need more distance to stop on a slippery road than on a dry road. Stay farther back when driving on slippery roads.

questions.question: Any alcohol in the blood can affect a driver's:

options.text: Right-of-way privileges.
Judgment and physical coordination.
Knowledge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and physical coordination.
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol can affect your ability to drive safely. It can harm your judgment and physical coordination. Driving after drinking any amount of alcohol can lead to criminal charges.

questions.question: Which of these commonly causes traffic crashes?

options.text: Driving above the speed limit or too fast for conditions.
Getting enough rest and staying alert.
Paying attention to the road and staying focused.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving above the speed limit or too fast for conditions.
questions.explanation: Speeding and driving too fast for road conditions commonly cause crashes. Always drive within the speed limit and adjust your speed for the conditions.

questions.question: Why is using a cell phone while driving a distraction?

options.text: It makes you worry about the cost of the call.
It takes your hands, eyes, and attention away from driving.
It distracts other drivers on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes your hands, eyes, and attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Cell phones distract drivers because they use your hands, eyes, and mind. Even good drivers increase their crash risk by using a cell phone while driving.

questions.question: When stopped by police, you must show:

options.text: Only your insurance and registration.
Only your license.
Your license, insurance, and registration.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your license, insurance, and registration.
questions.explanation: You must carry and show your license, registration, and insurance. All three documents are required when driving.

questions.question: Night driving is harder because:

options.text: The speed limit is higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the road at night.
It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.
questions.explanation: Night driving is difficult because you can only see as far as your headlights. This makes it hard to judge how far away other vehicles are and how fast they are going.

questions.question: If you have a tire blowout, you should:

options.text: Tap or pump the brakes.
Slow down gradually and brake lightly.
Brake hard and fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and brake lightly.
questions.explanation: If you have a blowout, take your foot off the gas and let the car slow down. Use the brakes lightly only after the car has slowed down a lot.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Drive carefully and be ready to stop.
You must come to a complete stop.
Stop only if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: The stop sign is the only eight-sided sign on the road. You must come to a complete stop. Do not go until it is safe to cross the intersection.

questions.question: Crashes are more likely when:

options.text: All vehicles are going about the same speed.
One lane is going faster than other lanes.
One vehicle is going faster or slower than the traffic flow.

questions.correctAnswerText: One vehicle is going faster or slower than the traffic flow.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other traffic. Speeding increases crash risk. Driving too slowly also causes crashes because other drivers may hit you or swerve to avoid you.

questions.question: Motorcycles are entitled to:

options.text: The same full lane width as other vehicles.
The width of the sidewalk.
Half the width of a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use the full lane width, just like any other vehicle.

questions.question: If the road is wet or icy, you should:

options.text: Slow down.
Drive at the posted speed.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: On wet or icy roads, your tires do not grip as well. Slow down so you can stop safely.

questions.question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, you should:

options.text: Make sure they see you, then go.
Drive around them carefully.
Stop and let them finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let them finish crossing.
questions.explanation: Always give pedestrians the right-of-way on the road, even without a marked crosswalk.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Anything that causes you to swerve.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind off the road. It is the most common cause of crashes. Distractions cause drivers to miss important sights and sounds that prevent crashes.

questions.question: Tailgating (driving too close behind another car):

options.text: Can anger other drivers.
Cannot result in a traffic ticket.
Stops other cars from cutting you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can anger other drivers.
questions.explanation: Tailgating frustrates drivers and can lead to aggressive driving. You can get a ticket for driving unsafely.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol or drugs?

options.text: Alertness.
Coordination.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs harm many driving skills, including reaction time, coordination, alertness, and concentration.

questions.question: At a crosswalk:

options.text: You must yield to pedestrians.
Pedestrians must yield to you.
Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crosswalks, but must follow traffic signals. Stop for pedestrians in any crosswalk, marked or unmarked.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Merge.
Road turns ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided red sign means stop.

questions.question: Blind spots are:

options.text: Areas where you lose vision when tired.
Areas you cannot see in your mirrors.
Traffic control devices.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas you cannot see in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check for blind spots. These are areas near the rear corners of your vehicle that your mirrors cannot show.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Pass as slowly as possible.
Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.
Pass as safely and as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass as safely and as quickly as possible.
questions.explanation: Pass quickly so you can return to your lane safely. Move back to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: A green traffic signal means you should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
Go straight, turn left, or turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go straight, turn left, or turn right.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can go straight or turn, if allowed. When turning on green, first let pedestrians and other vehicles in the intersection pass safely.

questions.question: On the freeway, when driving behind a large truck, you should:

options.text: Follow closer than you would behind a passenger vehicle.
Follow farther behind than you would behind a passenger vehicle.
Drive to the right side of the truck and wait to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow farther behind than you would behind a passenger vehicle.
questions.explanation: Follow farther behind large trucks because they have large blind spots where the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you must:

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Keep your normal speed.
Slow down and proceed carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means be alert and careful. Slow down before entering the intersection.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Have the right-of-way over oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to all oncoming traffic going straight. Always yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The road ends ahead.
The road splits. You must go right or left.
A four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road splits. You must go right or left.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you the road divides ahead. You must choose to bear right or left.

questions.question: A pedestrian is crossing your lane with no crosswalk. You should:

options.text: Make eye contact and pass the pedestrian.
Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians crossing your lane, even without a marked crosswalk. Always give pedestrians time to cross safely.

questions.question: To avoid losing traction on wet roads, you should:

options.text: Make sharp turns.
Press hard on the brakes.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on wet roads to prevent hydroplaning. Keep your tires in good condition. If you lose control, ease off the gas, do not brake, keep the wheel steady, and let the car slow down.

questions.question: Backing up your vehicle is:

options.text: Always dangerous.
Dangerous only if you have a helper.
Dangerous only in large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always dangerous.
questions.explanation: Backing is always risky because you cannot see clearly behind your vehicle. Use extra caution when backing up.

questions.question: At railroad crossings, you must watch for:

options.text: Vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings, like school buses and hazmat trucks.
Trains coming from either direction.
Both A and B.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B.
questions.explanation: Approach railroad crossings very carefully. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. Watch for vehicles that must stop at all crossings, like school buses and hazmat trucks.

questions.question: If railroad crossing gates are lowered and lights are flashing, you should:

options.text: Drive around the gates if you don't see a train.
Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then go when gates lift.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then go when gates lift.
questions.explanation: Stop at lowered crossing gates. It is illegal to drive around them. Wait until the gates are lifted before proceeding.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A 35 mph speed zone begins after the curve.
Drive at least 35 mph around the curve.
Slow to 35 mph or less before the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow to 35 mph or less before the curve.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts you to a curve ahead. The speed sign tells you the recommended safe speed for the curve.

questions.question: To pass safely on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Check how far away oncoming cars are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check how far away oncoming cars are.
questions.explanation: Judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles carefully. They may be closer or faster than they appear. Only pass if you are sure you have enough space and time to pass safely.

questions.question: Blue traffic signs provide information about:

options.text: Motorist services.
Construction and maintenance work.
Distances to specific locations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorist services.
questions.explanation: Blue signs tell you about services nearby, such as rest areas, food, gas, or hospitals.

questions.question: Which of these is a dangerous habit in work zones?

options.text: Tailgating another vehicle.
Not watching for workers and equipment.
Both A and B.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B.
questions.explanation: In work zones, reduce speed and keep distance from other vehicles. Watch carefully for workers and moving equipment.

questions.question: Which statement about large trucks is true?

options.text: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
They all have air brakes that stop quickly.
They are easier to maneuver than passenger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop. A passenger car at 55 mph stops in about 400 feet. The same truck at 55 mph needs almost 800 feet to stop.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: One outside mirror eliminates blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than passenger vehicles.
Your rearview mirror shows all blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: All vehicles have blind spots, even with mirrors. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than passenger cars.

questions.question: Never make sudden stops in front of large trucks because:

options.text: Small vehicle drivers cannot see large trucks in their mirrors.
Large trucks need more distance to stop due to their size and weight.
Large trucks travel faster than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks need more distance to stop due to their size and weight.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles take longer to stop and start than smaller cars. A sudden stop in front of a truck may cause a collision.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while driving, you should:

options.text: Hold the wheel firmly, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.
Pump the brakes quickly.
Brake hard and steer to the right edge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the wheel firmly, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: Stay calm when a tire blows. Grip the wheel firmly and ease off the gas to slow down. Lightly apply the brakes once the car has slowed. Move to the shoulder only after the vehicle is under control.

questions.question: You should drive on the shoulder to pass a car:

options.text: If the vehicle ahead is turning left.
Never.
If the shoulder is wide enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never pass on the shoulder. The other driver will not expect you there and may pull onto the shoulder, causing a crash.
